newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia rally helps Helsinki bourse to record close.
newsitem.headline: Nokia rally helps Helsinki bourse to record close.

text.p: Telecoms major Nokia rallied back on Wednesday to more than recover Tuesday's mild losses and led the Finnish bourse higher despite weakness in wholesaler Kesko and a sharp fall in bonds, brokers said.
The HEX all-share index rose 0.8 percent to a record-high close at 2,372.7 -- just 26.4 points or 1.1 percent off its all-time high set in intra-day trade last Friday.
Brokers saw further gains later this week, provided that the promising start on Wall Street at the time of the Finnish market's closing endured.

Nokia advanced 6.00 markka to end at 259.00. Brokers cited continued interest in the share after last week's encouraging third-quarter earnings report. On Wednesday, Nokia's slice of the Helsinki bourse's 440 million markka turnover was nearly half.

Finnish bonds fell in line with most European fixed income markets, but the weakness failed to depress finance sector stocks. Banking group Merita A hit a 17-month high 14.70 markka, but ended at 14.50 markka, up 0.10.
Wholesaler Kesko eased 0.70 markka to 61.80 after the European Union Commission -- as widely expected -- ruled against its merger with domestic rival Tuko.
Forest shares also bucked the broadly rising trend with UPM-Kymmene, Europe's biggest forest industry group, losing 0.40 markka to 89.00, and Enso falling 0.20 markka to 35.30.
